parts.text: Through Haggai, God addresses Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people who claim the time has not come to rebuild the temple. They have attended to their own houses while his lies ruined. Their harvests and earnings fail to satisfy because they neglect his house. He calls them to consider their ways, bring timber, and build so that he may be honored.

The governor, high priest, and remnant obey the LORD’s voice and fear before him. Haggai brings the assurance that God is with them. The LORD stirs their spirits, and they begin work on the house of their God. The chapter records the date when renewed obedience becomes practical labor.

chapters.title: Strength for the work and a promised blessing

parts.text: Those remembering the former temple’s glory are urged not to lose heart over the present work. God tells Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people to be strong because he is with them and his Spirit remains. He promises to shake heaven, earth, and the nations, fill the house with greater glory, and give peace there.

Questions to the priests show that uncleanness spreads while holiness is not automatically transferred. Haggai applies this to the people and their offerings, recalling the failed harvests of their disobedience. From this day God promises blessing. A final word to Zerubbabel announces the overthrow of kingdoms and declares that God has chosen him and will make him like a signet.
